customer_question: After an Android OS update changed our Host Subsystem and Profile Subsystem QDIDs, we need to update our End Product registration to reference the new Host-Core Configuration and Profile-layer QDIDs. Can your registration support service use a different company's existing test report as the evidence for this update, and what do we need to provide?
question_variants: Can we reuse a third party's test report when updating our registration after an OS-driven QDID change?
Is it acceptable to base a Host/Profile subsystem update on someone else's RF/RF PHY test report?
Does the age of a third-party test report matter for reuse in a registration update?
What do you need from us before you can check the new Host/Profile QDIDs for inter-layer consistency?
actual_issue: An Android OS update forced new Host Subsystem and Profile Subsystem QDIDs, and the customer wanted to update an End Product registration to reference them using a different company's previously-completed test report as supporting evidence, rather than commissioning new testing.
plain_english_explanation: When the operating system updates, the parts of a Bluetooth certification that describe the software layers (Host and Profile) can become outdated and need to be re-registered against newer reference IDs. The customer wanted to do this update using a test report that another company had already obtained, instead of paying for a brand-new test. The consultant confirmed this is allowed, as long as the report isn't too old relative to the current test requirements, and gave the customer a hard deadline and a heads-up about an upcoming rule change.
consultant_answer: Using another company's existing test report as evidence for the update is acceptable, consistent with prior guidance that a previous test report can support a new registration as long as too many years have not elapsed since it was produced. The consultant asked to be given the Design Numbers (DNs) of the newly-obtained Host-Core Configuration and Profile-layer QDIDs as soon as they are available, in order to check for inter-layer inconsistency against the rest of the design. The consultant also flagged that a new set of profile test items becomes effective on 2024-12-28 under TCRL2024-1, and recommended submitting the test report early so it can be checked in advance for whether it will remain usable as-is once that date passes.
decision_logic: A previously-produced test report (including one from a different company) remains valid evidence for a registration update as long as it is not too old relative to current requirements; the controlling constraints are (1) report age/recency relative to test-plan changes, and (2) inter-layer consistency between the newly-referenced QDIDs and the rest of the design, which can only be checked once the new DNs are known.
final_recommendation: Provide the DNs for the newly-obtained Host-Core Configuration and Profile-layer QDIDs as soon as they are issued so inter-layer consistency can be checked, and submit the third-party test report early -- ahead of the 2024-12-28 TCRL2024-1 effective date -- so it can be pre-checked for continued usability after the rule change takes effect.
risk_if_done_wrong: Submitting the report without an early pre-check risks discovering after the TCRL2024-1 effective date that the report no longer covers all required test items, and proceeding without supplying the new DNs risks an undetected inter-layer inconsistency surfacing later in the registration process.
